_meta.description: Quest dialogue for MQ-27: Coming Home. Year 3 Winter — resolution, NPC conclusions, sandbox transition.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The expedition returns to Coppervale on a clear winter morning. Word has already spread — the war is over. Every man, woman, and child in town has gathered at the eastern gate.]

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: THERE THEY ARE! Open the gates! OPEN THE GATES!

lines.speaker: npc_pip
lines.text: MISTER JACK! MISTER JACK! You came back! I KNEW you'd come back!

lines.speaker: npc_spark
lines.text: The mech looks like it went through a blender. A blender made of explosions. I love it. Welcome home, Jack.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: ...Welcome home, Jack.

lines.speaker: npc_kaydee
lines.text: Alright everyone — the Rusty Gear is open, the fires are lit, and I've been saving a very special barrel for this exact moment. Tonight, Coppervale CELEBRATES.

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: Before we celebrate... a moment. For those who aren't here to see this day. For the people we lost during the siege, and the brave souls who didn't make it back from the Spire.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [A moment of silence. Then Linden raises his glass.]

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: To Coppervale. To the future. And to the man who made it possible.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The town cheers. It echoes off the walls that held. Off the turrets that fired. Off the homes that survived. Coppervale endures.]

lines.speaker: npc_elm
lines.text: This is the third Remembrance Day. But this one is different. This is the first one where we light our lanterns not in defiance, but in peace.

lines.speaker: npc_elm
lines.text: We remember those who fell. We honor those who stood. And we look forward — to a future we earned with our own hands.

lines.speaker: npc_maren
lines.text: Oren, my love... you were right. This town had a future. I wish you could see it.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: I have 1.4 billion archived images of lantern ceremonies from before The Sundering. None of them look like this. None of them feel like this.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: I've been a soldier all my life, Jack. Fighting is all I knew. But watching this town grow... I think I've found something worth more than any battle. I'm staying. Not as your captain — as your neighbor.

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: The Council has formally recognized Coppervale as a regional capital. We're not just a settlement anymore — we're a beacon. And it all started with a broken workshop and one stubborn engineer.

lines.speaker: npc_spark
lines.text: Jack... the flyer works. I tested it this morning. I actually FLEW. It was only twelve seconds and I almost hit the chapel, but I FLEW! Next stop: the clouds!

lines.speaker: npc_maren
lines.text: I'm tired, dear. The good kind of tired. The kind that comes after a long day's work that meant something. Oren would be so proud of what you've built.

lines.speaker: npc_pip
lines.text: Mister Jack, I've been thinking. When I grow up, I want to be an engineer. Like you. Can you... can you teach me? For real this time?

lines.speaker: npc_leera
lines.text: You know, when you first arrived I thought you were just another soft-handed idealist who'd wash out in a month. Turns out you're the toughest person I've ever met. Don't let it go to your head.

lines.speaker: npc_michelle
lines.text: The clinic is expanding. Two rooms now, proper supplies, even a small surgery. For the first time in years, I'm not just patching people up — I'm actually healing them. Thank you, Jack. For everything.

lines.speaker: npc_kaydee
lines.text: The tavern's never been busier. Turns out people drink more when they're happy than when they're scared. Who knew? ...Okay, I knew. But it's nicer this way.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: I came here as a liaison. A bureaucratic assignment. I never expected to find... this. A home. People I'd fight for. Someone I'd...

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: ...Well. You know.

lines.speaker: npc_kiery
lines.text: I spent so long running. From place to place, never staying, never belonging. And then I came here, and you... you made me want to stay. For the first time, I'm not afraid of tomorrow.

lines.speaker: npc_paige
lines.text: I've been writing our story, Jack. All of it. The workshop, the siege, the expedition. Someday, when children ask how the world started over, I want them to know it began here. With us.

lines.speaker: npc_gus
lines.text: Business is booming! Three new trade routes, Thornwall importing our machine parts, Dusthaven sending the best grain you've ever tasted. The general store needs a bigger store!

lines.speaker: npc_ferris
lines.text: I've got radio contact with eleven settlements now. Eleven! We're building a communication network that spans the region. The world is getting smaller, Jack. In the best way.

lines.speaker: npc_hank
lines.text: The smithy's running three shifts now. Apprentices from Thornwall and Ironridge are coming to learn. Turns out Coppervale steel has a reputation. Not bad for a frontier forge.

lines.speaker: npc_bramble
lines.text: I've started writing a medical guide. Everything I've learned traveling, everything Michelle has taught me. If something happens to us, the knowledge survives. That matters.

lines.speaker: npc_elm
lines.text: The chapel is full every week now. Not from fear — from gratitude. People come to give thanks, to remember, to hope. That's all a pastor can ask for.

lines.speaker: npc_nora
lines.text: The kitchen feeds forty people a day now. Forty! And next spring I'm starting a community garden behind the tavern. Fresh vegetables for everyone.

lines.speaker: npc_wes
lines.text: Jack. Ellie and Tomm are safe. The allied forces found them during the Scorchland campaign. They're here now — in Coppervale. My sister is... she's here.

lines.speaker: npc_wes
lines.text: I'll never be able to repay what you did for me. Forgiving me when I didn't deserve it. Bringing my family home. I'll spend the rest of my life trying to be worthy of this town's trust.

lines.speaker: npc_nora
lines.text: Jack... a letter came. From Wes. He found his sister. They're safe, living in a settlement south of the Scorchlands. He says... he's sorry. And he hopes Coppervale is everything it deserves to be.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: The Council has the Marshal in custody. He's cooperating — grudgingly. His knowledge of Pre-War military infrastructure is invaluable. In time, he may become an advisor. Stranger things have happened.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Dorian Voss has chosen exile. He left for the northern territories three days ago. But before he went, he gave us everything — troop positions, supply caches, fortification blueprints. A final gift.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: He left a note for you, Jack. It says: 'You've proven a better way is possible. Do not fail to protect it.' I think, in his own way... he's grateful.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: Jack. Now that the AEGIS network is destroyed and the truth is known... I've been thinking about what I am. What I want to be.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: I was built as a weapon. I chose to be a tool. You made me a friend. But now... I think I want to be a historian.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: The Old World is full of knowledge — art, science, music, literature — buried in ruins and data cores. If we don't preserve it, it's gone forever. I want to make sure the next generation inherits more than just survival skills.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: DEJIN the Historian. I like it.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: Besides, someone needs to document the true story of Coppervale. And I have a rather excellent memory. When it's not being deliberately erased, that is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Winter fades. Spring returns to Coppervale — not the anxious spring of survival, but the hopeful spring of a new beginning. The walls still stand. The workshop hums. The town grows.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Jack stands at the Overlook, looking down at the town that started as a ruin and became a home. Somewhere below, Spark is shouting about a new invention. Harrow is drilling volunteers. Kaydee is pouring drinks. Life goes on.]

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: Jack? The rail network plans are ready for review whenever you are. Thornwall has already committed materials for the first line. The future isn't going to build itself.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: ...Actually, given our track record, it probably will. With considerable assistance from gears, steam, and stubbornness.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [The story of the war is over. The story of Coppervale continues.]
